question: A buyer who purchases a used watercraft may operate it on Ohio waters without a certificate of title for up to how many days, provided they have a dealer's dated bill of sale or a notarized casual-sale bill of sale in their possession?
explanation: Per ORC 1548.03, a purchaser may take possession of and operate a watercraft or outboard motor without a certificate of title for up to 60 days if in possession of a dealer's dated bill of sale, or in a casual sale, a notarized bill of sale.

question: After purchasing or otherwise acquiring ownership of a watercraft, within how many days must the buyer file an application for a certificate of title, and what late penalty fee applies if that deadline is missed?
explanation: ORC 1548.06(C) requires the title application to be filed within 30 days after the date of purchase or assignment of ownership; missing the deadline adds a $5 late penalty fee to the standard title fee.

question: Once a lienholder receives good funds that fully discharge a security interest noted on a titled watercraft, how many business days does the lienholder have to deliver the certificate of title, or a sworn statement of discharge, to the clerk?
explanation: ORC 1548.20(C) requires delivery of the certificate of title or a sworn discharge statement not more than seven business days after good funds fully discharging the security interest have been credited.

question: Under Ohio law, knowingly procuring or attempting to procure a certificate of title to a watercraft or outboard motor that the person has reason to believe was stolen is punishable as what level of offense?
choice_a: A misdemeanor of the first degree
choice_b: A felony of the third degree
choice_c: A minor misdemeanor, with no jail time possible
choice_d: A felony of the fifth degree
explanation: ORC 1548.19 prohibits procuring or passing a certificate of title to a watercraft or outboard motor known or believed to be stolen; ORC 1548.99 sets the penalty at a felony of the fifth degree.

question: Operating a watercraft on Ohio waters without a certificate of title, or on a certificate of title that has been canceled, is punishable as what level of offense?
choice_a: A misdemeanor of the fourth degree
choice_b: A felony of the fifth degree
choice_c: A misdemeanor of the first degree
choice_d: It is a civil infraction only, with no criminal penalty
explanation: ORC 1548.18 prohibits operating a watercraft without a certificate of title or on a canceled title; ORC 1548.99 sets the penalty at a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

question: Which of the following watercraft is exempt from Ohio's titling requirement regardless of its length or the horsepower of its motor?
choice_c: A 16-foot pontoon boat with a 25-horsepower motor
explanation: ORC 1548.01(B) exempts canoes from titling categorically, regardless of length or motor size -- unlike other small craft, which are only exempt if less than 14 feet long with a motor under 10 horsepower.

question: A watercraft owned by which of the following is exempt from Ohio's certificate-of-title requirement?
choice_a: A private individual who is an Ohio resident
choice_b: A watercraft dealership holding the boat for resale
choice_c: The United States, the state of Ohio, or a political subdivision of the state
choice_d: A rental company operating on an Ohio lake
explanation: ORC 1548.01(B) exempts a watercraft whose owner is the United States, a state, or a political subdivision of a state from Ohio's titling requirement.

question: When applying for a certificate of title, what choice does an Ohio watercraft owner have regarding the form of the certificate?
choice_a: Only a physical, paper certificate of title is available
choice_b: Only an electronic certificate is available; paper certificates have been eliminated
choice_c: The owner must obtain both a physical and an electronic certificate
choice_d: The owner may elect either a physical certificate of title or to have it recorded only in the electronic title system
explanation: ORC 1548.021 allows an owner to elect whether the clerk issues a physical certificate of title or maintains the title electronically in the automated system.

question: Under Ohio law, how may two people hold ownership of a titled watercraft so that, upon the death of one, full ownership automatically passes to the survivor?
choice_a: By establishing joint ownership with right of survivorship on the certificate of title
choice_b: This type of ownership arrangement is not available for watercraft titles in Ohio
choice_c: Only through a separate, court-approved trust document
choice_d: By each person holding a separate certificate of title for the same watercraft
explanation: ORC 1548.071 allows any two persons to establish joint ownership with right of survivorship in a watercraft or outboard motor for which a certificate of title is required.

question: Ohio law allows an owner of a titled watercraft to have ownership pass automatically to a chosen person upon the owner's death, without probate, by doing what?
choice_a: Naming the beneficiary in an unrelated will only
choice_b: Designating the watercraft or outboard motor in transfer-on-death beneficiary form on the certificate of title
choice_c: Filing a beneficiary form with the boat's insurance company
choice_d: Ohio law does not permit a transfer-on-death designation for watercraft
explanation: ORC 1548.072 allows an owner to establish transfer-on-death ownership of a titled watercraft or outboard motor by designating it in beneficiary form in accordance with ORC 2131.13.

question: When a minor under 18 years old is party to a watercraft certificate-of-title application, what must accompany that application?
choice_a: Nothing additional -- minors may sign title applications on their own
choice_b: A separate certificate of title issued solely in the parent's name
choice_c: A form signed by one of the minor's parents, the minor's guardian, or another person having custody of the minor
choice_d: Proof that the minor has completed a boater education course
explanation: ORC 1548.031 requires the title application to be accompanied by a form signed by one of the minor's parents, the minor's guardian, or another person having custody of the minor.

question: What is the standard fee for an original certificate of title for a watercraft or outboard motor issued by the clerk?
explanation: ORC 1548.10 sets the fee for each certificate of title at $15.

question: If an owner's certificate of title is lost or destroyed, what must the owner obtain, and what must it be marked as?
choice_a: A duplicate certificate of title, for a $15 fee, marked "duplicate"
choice_d: There is no duplicate title process -- the watercraft must be re-titled as new
explanation: ORC 1548.09 and 1548.13 provide for a duplicate certificate of title, issued for a $15 fee and marked "duplicate."

question: A watercraft or outboard motor acquired by its owner before January 1, 1964 is treated how under Ohio's titling law?
choice_a: It must still be titled immediately, with no exception
choice_b: It need not be titled until it is mortgaged, sold, or otherwise disposed of
choice_c: It is permanently and unconditionally exempt from titling forever, even after a future sale
choice_d: It must be titled only if it is over 26 feet long
explanation: ORC 1548.21 provides that a watercraft or outboard motor acquired by the owner before January 1, 1964 need not be titled until it is mortgaged, sold, or otherwise disposed of.

question: A watercraft from a country other than the United States that is temporarily using Ohio waters is treated how under Ohio's titling requirement?
choice_a: It must obtain an Ohio title within 60 days of entering Ohio waters
choice_b: It must obtain an Ohio title before entering Ohio waters at all
choice_c: It is exempt from Ohio's titling requirement
choice_d: It is exempt only if it is under 14 feet long
explanation: ORC 1548.01(B) exempts a watercraft from a country other than the United States that is temporarily using Ohio waters from the titling requirement.

question: A watercraft covered by a valid U.S. Coast Guard marine document (a "documented vessel") is treated how under Ohio's certificate-of-title law specifically?
choice_a: It must obtain an Ohio certificate of title in addition to its federal documentation
choice_b: It is completely exempt from every Ohio requirement, including registration
choice_c: It must surrender its federal documentation to obtain an Ohio title
choice_d: It is exempt from Ohio's certificate-of-title requirement, even though it must still be separately registered and display Ohio tags
explanation: ORC 1548.01(B) exempts a federally documented watercraft from Ohio's title requirement specifically. This is separate from ORC 1547.531, which still requires the vessel to be registered in Ohio and display two Ohio tags.

question: In a watercraft sale where a licensed, registered watercraft dealer is a party to the transfer, what requirement is waived that would otherwise apply to a casual (private) sale between two individuals?
choice_a: The notarization requirement on the certificate-of-title assignment
choice_b: The requirement to deliver a certificate of title at all
choice_c: The requirement to pay any title fee
choice_d: The requirement to complete a bill of sale
explanation: ORC 1548.061 waives notarization on the certificate of title, assignment, and related documents when a registered watercraft dealer is a party to the transfer -- unlike a casual sale, where ORC 1548.06 requires notarization.
